Diego to share Dedicated vs Private deployment performance matrix
Customer to confirm procurement timeline and budget by 2026-12-10

summary: Procurement intake with AltaStream to align on MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA tiers for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing approvals and pilot next steps. Legal raised data residency and KMS questions; engineering wants a performance benchmark comparing reserved capacity and private deployment. Action items and timelines captured.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-30
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Lina Ho (Redwood CSM), Jenna Lowe (AltaStream - Dir Sourcing), Marcus Chen (AltaStream - Head Eng), Priya Nair (AltaStream - Legal), Ethan Brooks (AltaStream - FinOps)

00:00:00 - Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 50 minutes, really appreciate you making time right before the holiday window. Quick rollcall?
00:00:10 - Jenna: Hi, this is Jenna, thanks.
00:00:12 - Marcus: Marcus here.
00:00:14 - Priya: Priya on legal.
00:00:16 - Ethan: Ethan, hi.
00:00:18 - Diego: Diego, SE from Redwood.
00:00:20 - Samira: Great. Purpose today is to walk procurement and legal through the MSA/DPA posture, clarify SLAs and deployment options and lock next steps for pilot and pricing path. I'll hand to Diego for a quick tech framing and then Priya we can pause for legal questions.

00:01:05 - Diego: Cool. I'll be brief. Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployment into a VPC or on-prem. For enterprise like AltaStream, common pattern is start with a Dedicated pool for predictable throughput and then move to Private if you need strict network controls or air-gapped. Key differences: data residency and key management—private gives you customer KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Dedicated is isolated but still in our infra; we sign DPAs and can offer contractual controls.
00:02:00 - Marcus: Quick clarifying q: when you say "private" does that always mean the control plane is customer-managed? Or is there a hybrid where control plane is in your cloud but data plane lives in our VPC?
00:02:20 - Diego: Good question. We have two patterns: private full (control plane boxed for the customer, can be on-prem or VPC with our installer) and hybrid where the control plane is utility-managed but data plane and model serving nodes live in your VPC, keys in your KMS. Hybrids are common to reduce operational lift.
00:02:45 - Priya: From legal viewpoint we need clarity on audit logs retention, encryption at rest, and whether logs containing prompts are accessible by Redwood ops.
00:03:05 - Samira: We can commit to a DPA clause that specifies log access: by default logs are retained for X days and access is restricted; for private deployments, logs remain customer-controlled. Samira: I'll follow up with exact retention windows but we can commit to role-based access and audit trails.
00:03:30 - Priya: What's your SOC 2 status and do you have an ISO cert?
00:03:40 - Diego: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; ISO is in flight, we also have penetration test reports we can redact and share under an NDA.
00:03:55 - Jenna: Procurement will need a copy of SOC 2 and a standard security questionnaire answered before we can go to legal review.
00:04:05 - Samira: We'll send the SOC2 and a completed security spreadsheet; Lina will coordinate.
00:04:12 - Lina: Yep I'll attach the security pack to the follow-up.

00:05:00 - Ethan: Price question — our FinOps team needs to understand committed vs usage pricing. If we do Dedicated reserve, is there a discount ladder or minimum term? Also curious about overage rules.
00:05:18 - Samira: For Dedicated we typically offer a 12-month reserved capacity contract with tiered pricing based on commit. There's also burst credits and overage is billed at a higher per-token rate; we can share an example pricing ladder. We can also show a hybrid pricing where private deployment includes platform fee + infra costs.
00:05:40 - Ethan: Do you support net-net pricing approvals or do you require PO up-front?
00:05:45 - Samira: Standard is PO for enterprise with monthly invoicing; for pilot we can do credit account or short-term invoice.

00:06:30 - Marcus: On performance — for inference latency sensitive features, how do you handle KV cache and long-context? We need benchmark numbers for 8k and 32k sequences for our internal eval.
00:06:45 - Diego: Absolutely. We have optimized kernels and KV cache support. Performance depends on model variant and quantization. I will run a small benchmark matrix comparing Dedicated vs Private on 8k sequences and share. Expect per-token latencies to be X-ish (diego mumbles numbers), but I'll put real numbers in the doc.
00:07:10 - Marcus: Cool. Also are you offering guaranteed p99 latency SLAs for Dedicated? Our SLAs for user-facing features require 200ms p95 target.
00:07:25 - Samira: We offer SLA tiers for Dedicated; p99 guarantees depend on model and configured SLOs. Typically we define throughput and latency SLOs in the SLA attachment. If 200ms p95 is the bar, we need to map model, sequence length, and concurrency — we can put that into the SLA.

00:08:00 - Priya: Back to the MSA/DPA. We looked at the standard MSA and DPA you provided. Two ask items: (1) Data residency — we need contractually guaranteed data residency in eu-west for all EU-paid customers, and (2) DPA must explicitly prohibit Redwood staff access to prompts and context except under customer escalation with documented justification.
00:08:30 - Samira: For residency we can add a residency clause and guarantee routes to eu-west for EU tenants. For staff access, for hosted we have strict escalation workflows; for private deployments, keys and logs are customer-controlled so we can grant that. I'll note that some hosted operations need ephemeral access for incidents but that's auditable.
00:08:55 - Priya: We'll need a vendor attestation for those escalation cases and an approval flow that includes our security team sign-off.

00:09:30 - Jenna: Timeline question — procurement wants to know the shortest path to a pilot that exercise the dedicated pool and the DPA review. Ideally start pilot in mid-December, finish contract by end of January. Is that feasible?
00:09:45 - Samira: Yes, plausible. If we get signoff on pricing and any major MSA redlines this week, legal can circulate final redline the following week. Pilot can start as soon as a PO or pilot credit is in place.

00:10:20 - Ethan: On pricing — one more nuance: do you offer committed spend that can be split across teams, or is it per-account? We have multiple product labs who want allocation.
00:10:35 - Samira: Commitments can be set at account or sub-account level; we can do internal metering and per-team reporting. We'll include a billing flow doc.

00:11:05 - Marcus: A technical question — when you do upgrades or rollouts, what's the rollback policy and how do canaries work? We can't have a breaking model swap mid-peak.
00:11:20 - Diego: Rollouts use canary slots with automatic fallback. We support pinning model versions per route. In Dedicated you control the rollout windows; canary traffic is routed gradually and if quality or latency regresses, automatic fallback happens. We'll share the rollout and tracing docs.

00:12:00 - Priya: Liability and indemnity — our counsel wants to cap liability and ensure IP indemnity clauses for outputs. Any previous customers pushback?
00:12:15 - Samira: We can discuss liability limits in the MSA; typical enterprise cap is set to fees paid in 12 months. For IP, there's nuance around user-provided data vs model outputs; we'll propose language but legal will need to negotiate.

00:13:00 - Jenna: Thought — we may need a redline call separate with legal to walk through the MSA line-by-line. Can we set that up?
00:13:08 - Samira: Absolutely, we can schedule a 60-minute redline session with our counsel and your legal. Lina will coordinate availabilities.

00:14:00 - (brief pause / side chatter)
00:14:30 - Diego: Quick note on encryption: for hosted we encrypt at rest and in transit; KMS integration (customer-managed) is available on Private and hybrid. For Dedicated we can support bringing your own KMS in some regions.
00:15:00 - Priya: If we bring our KMS keys, do you support HSM-backed keys and split-key approaches?
00:15:12 - Diego: Yes HSM-backed KMS is supported; split-key specifically would require implementation but we can discuss patterns.

00:16:00 - Ethan: Regarding billing and SSO — we require SAML SSO for admin portal and role-based billing views. Is that supported?
00:16:12 - Lina: SSO via SAML/SCO is supported, and RBAC is configurable. Billing views can be scoped by roles.
00:16:25 - Ethan: Great. We also track cost by route and token. Do you provide token-level breakdowns?
00:16:35 - Diego: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdown per model/route. We can maintain retention windows for metrics too.

00:17:10 - Marcus: For the pilot acceptance criteria we need: 1) performance within 10% of our current latency baseline, 2) no data exfiltration in logs, 3) billing visibility, and 4) ability to pin a model version. Can you commit to that?
00:17:30 - Samira: Those are reasonable pilot criteria. We'll include them in a pilot statement of work.

00:18:10 - Priya: One more DPA item — subprocessors list and notification obligations on changes.
00:18:20 - Samira: We'll share current subprocessor list and agree to notify for material changes; we can include a 30 day notification window in the DPA.

00:19:00 - Jenna: On procurement flow — once legal finishes redline, procurement needs an approved pricing deck + PO terms to run through our finance approvers. Can you send a clean pricing spreadsheet and an example PO?
00:19:18 - Samira: Yes, I'll send the pricing sheet and a sample PO template.

00:20:00 - (Diego explains sample architecture diagram, occasional crosstalk)
00:22:30 - Marcus: There's some confusion internally around model hosting costs vs infra. Can you provide a breakdown where model inference cost is separate from hosting and support?
00:22:45 - Samira: We'll provide a line-item pricing sheet: per-token inference, per-GPU-hour hosting, platform fee, and support tier fees.

00:24:00 - Priya: Can Redwood accept limited security audit by our third-party assessor? We may want to run a scoped pentest or audit.
00:24:12 - Diego: Scoped assessments are doable; for hosted we often do vendor attestation and provide test harness. For private, direct access can be arranged. We'll need a scoping doc and NDA.

00:25:30 - Jenna: If we proceed, who signs the MSA? Which title at Redwood?
00:25:40 - Samira: Our standard signer is the Head of Commercial or VP of Finance depending on the deal size. We'll route as needed.

00:26:15 - Ethan: On credits for pilot — can you do $20k credit or a 30-day free trial instance for us to test integration?
00:26:30 - Samira: We can offer pilot credits — I'll propose $15k credit with ability to extend based on usage; details in the pilot SOW.

00:27:10 - (discussion on procurement windows and internal approvers)
00:30:00 - Samira: Let's surface the key legal redlines now so we can capture them: Priya you mentioned residency, log access clause, subprocessors notification, and liability cap. Anything else?
00:30:15 - Priya: Also data retention windows, breach notification SLA (we want 72 hours), and requirement for SAML SSO audit logs.
00:30:28 - Samira: Noted: retention windows, breach notification 72 hours, SAML audit logs. We'll add to the checklist.

00:31:10 - Marcus: Operations — for Dedicated, what's the typical maintenance window and its notice?
00:31:20 - Diego: Maintenance windows are scheduled with at least 48 hours notice; for critical security patches we may do emergency work with best-effort notice but can commit to minimal downtime and rollback plans.

00:32:00 - Jenna: Are there any regulatory concerns for healthcare PHI if we wanted to send PHI through the API?
00:32:12 - Priya: We'll definitely need to scope that. PHI will likely push us to private deployment and stronger BAAs.
00:32:20 - Samira: We do offer BAAs and can support HIPAA workloads in private setups; we'll share compliance artifacts.

00:33:00 - (short pause)
00:33:30 - Diego: I'll summarize technical deliverables: benchmark numbers (8k/32k), KV-cache behavior doc, rollout/canary doc, KMS integration patterns.
00:33:45 - Samira: And commercial/legal deliverables: redlined MSA/DPA examples, clean pricing spreadsheet, sample PO, pilot SOW template, SOC2 and security pack.

00:34:20 - Priya: Let's lock a date for a legal redline session. Our counsel is available the week of 2026-12-07.
00:34:30 - Samira: That works. Lina will propose times for 2026-12-08 or 2026-12-09.

00:35:00 - Jenna: Procurement target — if legal signs off by mid-December and finance OKs budget, we can issue a PO by 2026-01-15.
00:35:12 - Ethan: Confirm budget approver list — I'll send names after the call.

00:36:00 - (some back and forth clarifying dates)
00:38:00 - Marcus: One question on fallback — if your capacity in a region is constrained, do you failover to another model or another region automatically? What are the controls?
00:38:15 - Diego: We have smart routing with policies. You can set policy preferring latency or cost; we also recommend canary and fallback model variants. Failover across regions can be automatic but may change latency and residency - that has to be controlled via policy.

00:39:30 - Priya: We will not accept automatic failover that violates residency.
00:39:40 - Samira: Understood — residency policies will be enforced and included in the SLA.

00:41:00 - (brief technical clarifications from Marcus)
00:44:00 - Samira: Ok let's recap next steps: (1) Samira sends redlined MSA & DPA examples + pricing sheet (due 2026-12-03), (2) Diego shares benchmark and KV-cache numbers (due 2026-12-06), (3) Lina shares SOC2 and security pack (ASAP), (4) schedule legal redline session for week of 2026-12-07. Priya to send any must-have contract language before redline session.
00:44:35 - Priya: I'll email the list of mandatory clauses.
00:44:40 - Samira: Great. Any final questions?
00:44:45 - Jenna: No, that covers it.
00:44:48 - Ethan: All good.
00:44:50 - Marcus: Thanks everyone.
00:44:55 - Samira: Thanks, we'll follow up with the materials and proposed times.
00:45:05 - (meeting ends, small noise)

Post-meeting notes: procurement timeline looks like mid-December pilot kickoff; legal redline week of 2026-12-07. Customer is leaning Dedicated initially with an eye toward Private for PHI. Notable redlines: residency, log access, breach notice, subprocessors notifications, liability cap. Pilot credits asked ~$15k (TBD).
